key_insight: Eigenvalue-based neural constitutive models jointly learn yield functions and evolution laws while enforcing isotropy, convexity, and thermodynamic consistency by construction.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables flexible, data-driven modeling of rate-independent isotropic elastoplasticity for finite element analysis, including non-associative flow.
method: Use permutation-invariant spectral representations to enforce isotropy and convexity.
Represent non-associative yielding through a convex flow potential plus a jointly trained additive term.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit differentiation with eigenvalue-degeneracy safeguards.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes reproducing known constitutive models, learning from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam responses, and solving plane-stress boundary-value problems.
watch_item: Implementation requires robust implicit return-map solves and careful differentiation near repeated eigenvalues.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
